data.name: Battle Focus
data.summary: Start each battle round with the Battle Focus allocation for the game size. Unspent tokens expire at the end of that battle round.
conditions: Army rule must apply. Strike Force grants 4 tokens; Incursion 2; Onslaught 6.
Spending a token needs a matching Agile Manoeuvre trigger. Each unit normally performs at most one per phase; each manoeuvre is normally once per phase unless stated otherwise.
data.question: Do these tokens refresh at the start of both players’ turns?
data.answer: No. The allocation is per battle round. This reminder appears before the first player’s Command phase, not before every Command phase.

data.name: Diviner of Futures
data.summary: Eldrad adds 1 CP at the start of your Command phase if he is on the battlefield.
conditions: Not merely present in the roster: Eldrad must be on the battlefield.
This is additional to the Core CP both players gain in the following step.
data.question: Does Eldrad generate this CP in the opponent’s Command phase?
data.answer: No. His rule specifies the start of your Command phase.

data.name: Doom
data.summary: At the end of your Movement phase, Eldrad can select a visible enemy within 18 inches. Friendly Aeldari attacks against that target receive +1 to wound until the start of your next Command phase.
conditions: Check Eldrad’s battlefield presence, visibility and range when selecting the target.
Only attacks against the selected enemy get this effect; apply normal modifier rules.
data.question: Is Doom limited to your Shooting phase?
data.answer: Its stated duration extends beyond that phase. Check the target and the expiry at the start of your next Command phase.

data.name: Whirling Death
data.summary: While Jain Zar leads the unit, an Advance uses a fixed 6-inch increase instead of an Advance roll, and its Advance movement ignores vertical distance.
conditions: Jain Zar must still be leading the unit.
This changes the Advance; it does not make the unit’s full move distance 6 inches.
data.question: Can you reroll the Advance roll here?
data.answer: There is no Advance roll when this rule replaces it. Check other modifiers and restrictions separately.

data.name: Superlative Strategist
data.summary: While the Autarch leads a unit, that unit may reroll Advance rolls and rolls made while performing an Agile Manoeuvre.
conditions: Applies only while leading.
An Advance-roll reroll cannot be used when another rule means no Advance roll is made.
data.question: Does this automatically reroll any movement-related die?
data.answer: No. The wording identifies Advance rolls and rolls during an Agile Manoeuvre, not every movement-related roll.

data.name: Flickerjump
data.summary: When selected for a Normal move in your Movement phase, the Spiders can use a 24-inch Move characteristic. They cannot declare a charge that turn, and must resolve the ability’s end-of-phase risk.
conditions: Choose at the Normal-move selection window.
At the end of the phase roll once per model; each 1 inflicts a mortal wound on the unit.
data.question: Is this simply a longer move with no tradeoff?
data.answer: No. Remember both the charge restriction and the pending risk roll, even if the move itself is already finished.

data.name: Flickerjump: resolve the risk
data.summary: If this unit used Flickerjump, now roll a D6 per model; each result of 1 causes one mortal wound to the unit.
conditions: Only if Flickerjump was actually used this phase.
The charge restriction still lasts until the end of the turn.
data.question: Should a unit that chose an ordinary Normal move roll?
data.answer: No. This consequence is conditional on using Flickerjump.

data.name: Grenade Pack Flyover
data.summary: Once per turn, after setup or after a Normal, Advance or Fall Back move, a Hawks unit can pick a visible enemy within 8 inches. Roll per Hawks model; 4+ results inflict mortal wounds, capped at 6.
conditions: This is in your Movement phase.
After using it, that unit cannot be targeted by the Explosives Stratagem for the rest of the turn.
data.question: Do you count an attached character as a Swooping Hawk model?
data.answer: The roll count specifies Swooping Hawks models. Check the model identities rather than assuming every model in an attached unit counts.

data.name: Swift as the Wind
data.summary: A Battle Focus option at selection for a Normal, Advance or Fall Back move increases the models’ Move characteristic by 2 inches for the phase.
conditions: Spend a token on an eligible Battle Focus unit.
This manoeuvre may be used more than once in a phase with different units; the per-unit manoeuvre limit still applies.
data.question: Does a move-end trigger let you apply this retroactively?
data.answer: No. This choice is at move selection.

data.name: Flitting Shadows
data.summary: A Battle Focus option can prevent enemy Fire Overwatch against the selected unit for the rest of the turn.
conditions: Trigger: selection for a Normal, Advance or Fall Back move, setup on the battlefield, or declaring a charge.
Spend a token, check the unit’s eligibility and the phase limits.
data.question: Can you wait for Overwatch to resolve and then cancel it?
data.answer: No. Use the stated trigger window, not a later attack result.

data.name: Star Engines
data.summary: When an eligible Vehicle is selected to Advance, this Battle Focus option gives its ranged weapons Assault until the turn ends.
conditions: Requires the Vehicle keyword, Battle Focus eligibility and a token.
The trigger is Advance selection, not after shooting.
data.question: Does this grant Assault to passengers as well?
data.answer: The effect describes the vehicle unit’s weapons. Do not extend it to a different unit without a rule doing so.

data.name: Opportunity Seized
data.summary: After an enemy finishes a Fall Back move, an eligible non-Titanic Battle Focus unit that began the phase engaged with it can use this manoeuvre for a D6+1-inch Normal move.
conditions: Spend a token and check the phase’s manoeuvre limits.
The response is after the enemy move ends. The starting engagement condition still matters.
data.question: Can any nearby unit make this response?
data.answer: No. The rule requires the responding unit to have started the phase engaged with that enemy.

data.name: Fade Back
data.summary: Just after an enemy shoots, a qualifying non-Titanic Battle Focus unit hit by those attacks can spend a token for a D6+1-inch Normal move.
conditions: Requires a hit, not necessarily a lost wound.
Check all eligibility and phase-use restrictions before moving.
data.question: Can you save this response until every enemy unit has shot?
data.answer: No. It is a just-after-this-unit-shoots window.

data.name: Sudden Strike
data.summary: At the end of a qualifying charge move, this Battle Focus manoeuvre raises the unit’s pile-in and consolidation distance to 6 inches for the turn.
conditions: A completed charge move and an available token are required.
Distance changes do not remove the movement’s other conditions.
data.question: Do you activate it when selecting a unit to fight?
data.answer: No. Its trigger is when that unit’s charge move ends.

data.name: Path of the Warrior
data.summary: When an eligible Aspect Warriors or Avatar of Khaine unit is selected to shoot or fight, choose rerolls of hit rolls of 1 or wound rolls of 1 for that unit until the phase ends.
conditions: Requires Aspect Host and the appropriate unit keyword or Avatar identity.
Make the selection at the ability’s trigger, not after seeing attack results.
data.question: Does the unit receive both rerolls automatically?
data.answer: No. This rule offers a choice. Your exported enhancement is Aspect of Murder, not Mantle of Wisdom, which is a separate rule.

data.name: Hand of Asuryan
data.summary: Once in the battle, when Asurmen is selected to shoot, his Bloody Twins can gain Damage 3, Anti-Infantry 5+ and Devastating Wounds for that phase.
conditions: The effect applies to his specified weapon, not every model in his attached unit.
Declare at selection to shoot; keep track of whether the battle-use remains.
data.question: Does it improve the Dire Avengers’ catapults too?
data.answer: No. Its weapon scope is Asurmen’s Bloody Twins.

data.name: Bladestorm
data.summary: Ranged weapons in the unit gain Sustained Hits 1 against a target within half range.
conditions: Check half range for the relevant weapon and target.
Any attached-model interactions and existing keywords still need the current rules applied.
data.question: Is half range measured once for the whole army?
data.answer: No. Check the attacking weapon’s range and the target.

data.name: Aspect Shrine Token
data.summary: A remaining token can turn one hit or wound result for a non-Character model in that unit into an unmodified 6. Each token is available once per battle.
conditions: The unit must actually have an unspent Aspect Shrine Token.
Character models are explicitly excluded, including attached leaders.
data.question: Can a token improve Asurmen’s own roll?
data.answer: No. He is a Character even when attached to Dire Avengers. Token count belongs to the equipped unit, not every model.

data.name: Inescapable Accuracy
data.summary: For the unit’s ranged attacks, you may ignore any or all modifiers to Ballistic Skill and to the hit roll.
conditions: This does not automatically ignore other defensive rules, saving throws or damage reductions.
data.question: Can you ignore a damage modifier with this ability?
data.answer: No. Its scope is Ballistic Skill and hit-roll modifiers.

data.name: Assured Destruction
data.summary: In your Shooting phase, attacks against a Monster or Vehicle unit can reroll hit, wound and damage rolls.
conditions: The target must have one of those qualifying keywords.
Apply the rule to the specified ranged attacks, not every future attack.
data.question: Does it grant the same rerolls against ordinary infantry?
data.answer: Not on the basis of this ability. Confirm the target’s keywords.

data.name: Crystalline Targeting
data.summary: After the Walkers shoot, choose an enemy they hit. Friendly Aeldari attacks against it improve AP by 1 until this phase ends.
conditions: There must have been a hit on the selected enemy.
Each enemy unit can be selected for this ability only once per turn.
data.question: Why might you choose the Walkers earlier in the shooting order?
data.answer: Their marked target can help subsequent Aeldari attacks. The effect does not retroactively change attacks already resolved.

data.name: Fire Support
data.summary: After the Falcon shoots, choose an enemy it hit. Friendly models that disembarked from that Falcon this turn may reroll wounds against that enemy until the turn ends.
conditions: The benefiting models must have disembarked from this transport this turn.
The target must have been hit by the Falcon’s attacks.
data.question: Does a nearby Fire Dragons unit qualify without disembarking?
data.answer: No. Proximity alone does not meet the passenger condition.

data.name: Tactical Acumen
data.summary: While Asurmen leads the unit, after it shoots in your Shooting phase it can make a Normal move of up to 6 inches. Taking that move prevents charging for the rest of the turn.
conditions: Asurmen must still be leading.
This is a move after that unit shoots, not the end-of-phase window.
data.question: Can the unit shoot, take this move, then charge?
data.answer: Not under this rule: choosing its move adds a charge restriction.

data.name: Acrobatic
data.summary: Howling Banshees can declare a charge after Advancing or Falling Back that turn.
conditions: This exception addresses those two move types.
It does not cancel a separate charge prohibition from a disembark mode or another ability.
data.question: Can “advance and charge” override every other restriction?
data.answer: No. Read the scope of each exception and each remaining restriction.

data.name: The Bloody-Handed
data.summary: Friendly Aeldari units within 6 inches of the Avatar receive +1 on Advance and Charge rolls.
conditions: Check the aura’s distance when applying the roll modifier.
A fixed movement replacement is not an Advance roll.
data.question: Does Jain Zar’s fixed Advance become an Advance roll?
data.answer: No. A fixed replacement and a roll modifier are different mechanics.

data.name: Molten Form
data.summary: When an attack is allocated to the Avatar, its Damage characteristic is halved.
conditions: Apply the current rounding and damage-modifier rules.
This is a defensive rule, not a blanket halving of every source of mortal wounds.
data.question: When should you check this?
data.answer: At allocation of an attack to the Avatar, in either player’s turn.

data.name: Wave Serpent Shield
data.summary: A ranged attack with Strength greater than this model’s Toughness suffers −1 to its wound roll against the Wave Serpent.
conditions: Compare Strength with Toughness; equality does not meet the condition.
This is ranged-only, and normal modifier rules still apply.
data.question: Does an equal-Strength attack trigger the shield?
data.answer: No. The comparison is strictly greater.

data.name: Fights First
data.summary: The Banshees and Jain Zar have Fights First. The Autarch gains it from Aspect Training while leading Howling Banshees. A unit needs every model to have it for the unit-level rule.
conditions: The Autarch’s Banshee attachment must still apply.
The current Fight sequence determines selection order; Fights First does not mean you always pick before the active player.
data.question: Why does the Autarch’s attachment matter?
data.answer: The relevant part of Aspect Training provides Fights First while leading Banshees. Do not assume the unattached model has that ability.

data.name: Storm of Silence
data.summary: Jain Zar may reroll wound rolls for her attacks targeting a Character unit.
conditions: Check the target unit’s keyword and which model is attacking.
This rule does not itself give Precision.
data.question: Does a reroll against a Character unit let you allocate directly to its leader?
data.answer: No. Targeting an attached unit and assigning wounds to its Character are distinct rules.

data.name: Aspect of Murder
data.summary: Your equipped enhancement adds 1 to the bearer’s melee-weapon Damage and gives those weapons Precision.
conditions: Only show this as equipped when the export lists Aspect of Murder.
Precision still requires its own allocation and visibility conditions.
data.question: Does it modify the Banshees’ weapons?
data.answer: No. The enhancement is scoped to the bearer’s melee weapons.

data.name: Path of Command
data.summary: Once per battle round across the army, a model with this rule can reduce a Stratagem’s cost by 1 CP when its unit is targeted.
conditions: It must be that model’s unit being targeted.
The battle-round allowance is shared across models with the ability.
data.question: Can the Autarch discount a Stratagem targeting a different unit?
data.answer: Not from this wording. Check the exact target and any cost-modifier rules.

data.name: Khaine’s Vengeance
data.summary: Aspect Host has a reaction when a non-Monster, non-Vehicle enemy is selected to Fall Back from an eligible Aspect Warriors or Avatar unit. Consult the Stratagem for the escape-test instructions.
conditions: This is selection to Fall Back, earlier than Opportunity Seized’s move-end trigger.
Check CP cost, current target eligibility and Battle-shock effects in your reference.
data.question: Are these two Fall Back reactions the same window?
data.answer: No. One is at selection; the other is after the move finishes.

data.name: Skyborne Sanctuary
data.summary: At the end of Fight, Aspect Host can use this Stratagem to embark an eligible unengaged Asuryani unit that was eligible to fight, if wholly within 6 inches of a compatible transport.
conditions: Transport eligibility and available capacity still matter.
Check CP cost and the exact current Stratagem before declaring it.
data.question: Can any unit near a transport use it?
data.answer: No. The unit must also have been eligible to fight and satisfy the unengaged, faction, and embark conditions.

data.name: Before selecting an attacker
data.summary: Aspect Host has before-selection options such as Warrior Focus. In your Shooting phase, Preternatural Precision and Doom Inescapable may also be relevant.
conditions: These are not automatic effects. Check the full Stratagem, CP cost, eligible target and timing.
Preternatural Precision uses Aspect Warriors; Doom Inescapable uses the Avatar.
data.question: Should you decide after rolling the unit’s attacks?
data.answer: No. Check the before-selection window. These reminders are reference prompts, not complete Stratagem instructions.

data.name: To Their Final Breath
data.summary: Aspect Host offers a fight-on-death reaction just after an enemy selects attack targets, for an eligible targeted Aspect Warriors or Avatar unit.
conditions: Check the full Stratagem for its roll, timing, token option, CP cost and the requirement that the destroyed model has not fought.
This card is a timing reminder, not the full resolution procedure.
data.question: Can it let a model that already fought fight again?
data.answer: Do not assume so. Its condition explicitly concerns models that have not fought this phase.

data.name: Deep Strike
data.summary: For an ingress move, a unit whose every model has Deep Strike can use its alternate setup option, more than 8 inches horizontally from enemy units, including in the enemy deployment zone.
conditions: Check when that ingress move is permitted and all applicable setup restrictions.
An attached model without the ability can matter to the every-model condition.
data.question: Is Deep Strike an extra unrestricted move after arriving?
data.answer: No. It changes the setup option for an ingress move; do not add a further move without another rule.

data.name: Unused Battle Focus expires
data.summary: At the end of the battle round, discard unspent Battle Focus tokens. The next allocation belongs to the next round’s opening.
conditions: This is after the second player’s turn, not after each Fight phase.
data.question: Can you carry an unspent token into the next round?
data.answer: Not under the Battle Focus rule reviewed here.

data.name: Deadly Demise
data.summary: When a model with Deadly Demise is destroyed, resolve any emergency passenger disembarkation first, then check its demise roll. A 6 causes the listed mortal-wound amount to nearby units.
conditions: Use the destroyed model’s printed Deadly Demise value; units from both sides can be affected.
This is a destruction trigger, not an ability to use whenever you attack.
data.question: Does every vehicle automatically explode?
data.answer: No. Check whether the model has the ability and whether its die result triggers it.

data.question: Does a separate Fuegan elsewhere in your army extend this unit’s range?
data.answer: No. Being in the same army is not enough; the leading relationship is required.
